region: Chamery · Montagne de Reims, Champagne, France
about: The Bonnet family has grown grapes in Chamery, on the western slopes of the Montagne de Reims, since 1862, when Grégoire Bonnet became one of the village’s first growers to make his own Champagne. The Bonnet-Ponson name dates from 1956, when André Bonnet married Monique Ponson, whose family farmed in neighbouring Vrigny. Today Thierry Bonnet works alongside his son Cyril, a trained oenologist who joined in 2013 and converted the family’s roughly ten hectares, spread over some fifty parcels, to organic farming, certified in 2016.

This is not a sparkling wine but a rare still red from Champagne, sold under the Coteaux Champenois appellation. It is pure Meunier from organically farmed plots in Chamery, on calcareous clay over sands and fossil shells. The grapes go into the vat as whole bunches, stems and all, and macerate for about ten days before fermenting with wild yeasts. The wine then rests for a little over a year in sandstone eggs and a 400-litre cask, and is bottled unfined, unfiltered and without added sulphur.

Expect a bright cherry-red wine, light on its feet. The German importer describes sweet cherry, plum and raspberry on the nose with a faint yeasty, lactic note, and a juicy, lively palate given a fine-grained grip by the whole-bunch stems. It is the kind of red that reveals how expressive Meunier can be when it is not turned into bubbles.
facts: Still red wine (Coteaux Champenois), not sparkling
12–13 months in sandstone eggs and a 400-litre cask
Certified organic; no added sulphur, unfined, unfiltered
